reviews.text: Un vrai film de voituuuuure. La VF a rendu le truc encore plus cliché mais j’ai quand même passé un plutôt bon moment. La fin était sympa, elle relève un peu le tout qui est très très prévisible. Y’a des scènes super belle et j’ai kiffé l’esthétique du film

“Ford v Ferrari” ?  More like “Snore I’m Sorry” Not for me… Racing scenes are cool, the Ford GT looks amazing. But maaaaan I could not get behind the script/dialogue. It was so on-the-nose, so melodramatic, and so bland. Each character felt like a caricature of what they should be playing - especially the Ford executives. I didn’t buy the manufactured drama between Ford and Miles, or the friendship between Shelby and Miles. I know it’s objectively better than 2.5 stars. But I had to struggle to get through this. A rare case of the instagram edits being better than the actual movie

ok so first and foremost yes i watched this because a man put it on for me. that is obvious. but let’s discuss this. ALL PERSONAL OPINIONS! the 2.5 hour runtime is no fucking joke here it absolutely feels like a 2.5 hour long movie. genuinely feels incredibly grating at times and truly does feel like a LONG movie. could be bad pacing issues, but could also certainly be because i don’t find this subject to be at all interesting. this is also made for a very specific type of person which is not me whatsoever, which i can usually find lots of enjoyment in films of that nature but for this one, i feel it is hard to feel connected to the story if you are not already interested in cars/racing. for someone like me who has little to no interest in either subject, it is extremely hard to digest and comes across as very boring during all of the scenes that are not either the business plotline or ken’s family’s plotline. car go fast vrroom!! is not interesting on its own without prior knowledge for someone like me. as for the things i did like about this movie, i felt as though it was quite well made! this is a very good film on a technical aspect, with very good sound, colouring, shots etc. and i liked the soundtrack! big fan of 60s. 2.5 stars, not for me at all, but could understand why someone would really like it.

There are 2 main things that the movie does not explain which limits my ability to care or get invested in the outcome of the movie. 1: Why Ferrari? The movie is Ford v Ferrari but they are barely mentioned at all, and are more a vague boogyman rather than an actual competitor or villian. They get bought by Fiat, and they are basically never mentioned or seen again till the end of the film. 2: What's the deal with Le Mans over any other race? They explained why the track is different the other race tracks, but never got me to understand why its more important than the Sebring or the Daytona. Even the movie puts more stakes on the Daytona race. There's a ton of plot how a big automobile companies treat both their workers and their racers, which is well done, and that should have been the focus of the movie if they weren't going to answer my uncultured questions.

This is a very straightforward Hollywood movie, but it’s one that actually tries. There’s still tells - plot points will be repeated four times so that anyone watching while staring at their phone can keep up, the plot is predictable, the acting bounces between “sufficient” and “actually good” depending on the scene, and the antagonists are a one-note caricature of capitalism. But there’s some good stuff to fight against that! The film is excellently shot, with some really stellar camera work that caught my attention. And it’s a movie about racing that absolutely nails the tension and pacing needed to make something like that work. So it’s at least worth the watch.

Unfortunately, I've done this film no favors by watching it immediately after Stanley Kubrick's impeccable Barry Lyndon. This is a very formulaic film; to be honest, if not for the two leads, I think this film would be very forgettable. But it's Damon and Bale's performances that sell this thing and elevate it above where it has any right to be. I need not really rip into this film too much, because if you have seen any sports or racing movie, you have probably already seen everything this film has to offer done better before.

Not a car person so the racing didn’t do much for me. Great racing scenes but everything else felt formulaic and strangely passionless for a movie about passionate people fighting corporate soullessness. Ford doesn’t care who wins, they just want a good photo. Ironically, that’s exactly how this movie felt to me.
Honestly, the movie would probably be a 7 or 8 out of 10, but it dragged on a bit for me. I think it could have been much shorter. But all in all, it was interesting to watch, and stressful too.

It's a good enough film. A based on real events story, a fun set of antagonists, all star cast. It just fell in the category of films that are not badly made in any way, but are also not meant for me, and do not have any sort of ground breaking element to the filmmaking that makes up for my lack of interest. A good film to watch while talking to your mom about interior design and Outlander. I do think Noah Jupe, playing Peter Miles, is one to watch though. His performance was still memorable while standing next to Damon, Bales, and Balfe. Which is terribly impressive for a 14ish year old.

Tristemente una decisiones narrativas bastante pobres son los que hacen chocar a esta película. Do you remember that heinous looking hairless chihuahua who won the World’s Ugliest Dog contest back in the 2000’s? I loved that crazy looking beast. I like all dogs but most of my favorite ones are weird looking and/or problematic. A pitbull that bites children and eats coffee tables because that’s just who it is, an English bulldog that can’t stop humping your guests, bull terriers with that Alien xenomorph shaped head. I prefer my movies to be like that too for the most part. I can’t really say anything bad about Ford V Ferrari because despite not being able to lose my awareness of the actors acting and not transforming into their characters. This thing is pretty clean and does exactly what it’s aiming to do. How much that affects you depends on who you are and what you’re into I guess. For me this movie was a big dopey Yellow Lab.
